profile.campus: Vantage San Antonio Campus (Texas Research Park)
profile.reading:
This building, TX11, is located at 14720 Omicron Drive in the Texas Research Park area of San Antonio, TX; Vantage does not publish this campus on its own site at all (no location page and no press release appear in vantage-dc.com's sitemaps), so this entry relies on secondary sourcing: Data Center Dynamics reporting on the building permit and San Antonio Report coverage of Vantage's underlying land purchase. TX11 was filed for permit in December 2023 at a stated construction cost of roughly $96 million, covering approximately 242,665 square feet across two stories with 32 megawatts of power, and was expected to reach completion in early 2026 per the permit timeline. No certifications are published, consistent with the building's pre-completion/under-construction status as of this research.

Vantage acquired 57.9 acres on Omicron/Theta Drive from the University of Texas System Board of Regents in July 2023, and a separate 31 acres at State Highway 151/Wiseman Boulevard in August 2023, forming two San Antonio sub-campuses: Texas Research Park (Omicron Drive, home to TX11 and TX12) and Westover Hills (Rogers Road, home to TX21 and TX22). This San Antonio campus is distinct from Vantage's much larger "Frontier" mega-campus, a separate $25 billion, 1.4-gigawatt, 3.7-million-square-foot, 1,200-acre development in rural Shackelford County, Texas, announced in August 2025 to meet AI demand.

San Antonio's data center growth, including Vantage's TX cluster, has concentrated on the city's West and Northwest sides where CPS Energy, the nation's largest municipally owned combined electric and gas utility, has courted large industrial and data center loads with dedicated substations and negotiated rate agreements. Bexar County and the City of San Antonio have both offered property-tax abatement agreements to data center developers as part of a broader economic-diversification push beyond the city's traditional military and tourism base. CPS Energy's long-range integrated resource planning has specifically flagged data centers as a fast-growing large-load category requiring new generation and transmission investment through the early 2030s, a dynamic Texas's ERCOT grid operator has also cited statewide as it revises long-term demand forecasts upward and weighs new large-load interconnection rules for data centers.

reading.body:
Vantage TX11 is a 32 megawatt, 242,665 square foot facility under construction at 14720 Omicron Drive in San Antonio's Texas Research Park, with targeted completion in early 2026. The operator does not publish specifications for this campus on its own website; these figures come from Data Center Dynamics reporting on a December 2023 building permit filing with a stated construction cost of roughly $96 million. No certifications are published, consistent with the building's pre-completion status.

At a common AI training density of 40 kilowatts per rack, this facility's 32 megawatt IT load translates to approximately 800 racks. TX11 is one of four Vantage buildings planned across two San Antonio sub-campuses acquired from the University of Texas System and private owners in mid-2023, distinct from Vantage's separately announced 1.4-gigawatt Frontier mega-campus in rural Shackelford County. Individually, TX11 would rank 19th among the 18 facilities in Texas with published megawatt figures, though the three other San Antonio campus buildings' capacities are not published and total San Antonio data center capacity across all operators remains undisclosed.

CPS Energy, San Antonio's municipal utility and the nation's largest municipally owned combined electric and gas utility, has actively courted large data center loads with dedicated substations and negotiated rates, and has flagged data centers in its long-range resource planning as a fast-growing category requiring new generation and transmission investment through the early 2030s. The city and Bexar County offer property-tax abatement to data center developers as part of economic diversification. Whether TX11's power can be reliably sourced and when the facility will accept load are not published.
